title: Instructions Are Evidence, Not Objectives: Measuring Outcome Alignment of Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.17757v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model agents can follow complex human instructions to solve real-world tasks. In practice, however, initial instructions are often incomplete. In our analysis of 100 user-agent trajectories from SWE-chat, 56\% of initial instructions omit requirements that later emerge as necessary, and 52\% of the useful follow-up requirements could have been inferred from the project. A user states requirements from their own understanding of the task, and these \textbf{stated requirements} often differ from the \textbf{true requirements} that completing the task imposes. An agent should therefore treat the instruction as evidence rather than as the objective, inferring the true requirements from the instruction and the environment and satisfying them even when the user is not yet aware of all of them. translated_title: 指令是证据，而非目标：衡量智能体的结果对齐能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型智能体能够遵循复杂的人类指令来完成现实世界的任务。然而在实践中，初始指令往往是不完整的。在我们对来自SWE-chat的100条用户-智能体交互轨迹的分析中，56%的初始指令遗漏了后来被证明是必要的需求，而52%的有用后续需求本可以从项目本身推断出来。用户根据自己对任务的理解来陈述需求，这些“陈述需求”往往不同于完成任务所真正要求的“真实需求”。因此，智能体应当将指令视为证据而非目标，从指令和环境中推断出真实需求，即使用户尚未意识到全部需求，也要予以满足。我们将这种能力称为“结果对齐”。在这项工作中，我们构建了TiGanEval，一个软件工程领域的基准测试……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出智能体应将用户指令视为“证据”而非“目标”，通过指令和环境推断出真实需求并予以满足（即“结果对齐”能力），并构建了TiGanEval基准来衡量这一能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes that agents should treat instructions as evidence rather than objectives, inferring true requirements from both instructions and the environment (termed "outcome alignment"), and introduces TiGanEval, a benchmark to measure this ability.
